newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain and Morocco to cooperate on drugs.
newsitem.headline: Spain and Morocco to cooperate on drugs.

text.p: Spain and Morocco agreed on Thursday to tighten cooperation on illegal immigration and drug trafficking, two sources of tension between the neighbouring states.

Spanish Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja and his Moroccan opposite number Driss Basri, meeting in Madrid, decided to establish several joint committees to monitor illegal immigration to Spain and the drug trade.
"I'm convinced there will be a new era in which we will perfect the solution of concrete problems betweeen Spain and Morocco," Oreja said in a news conference on Thursday.
The flow of illegal immigraants into Spain has increased significantly since 1991 when Madrid first introduced a visa requirement for visiting Moroccans.
The two countries have a long history of trade and are geographically linked through Spain's two enclaves on the North African mainland.
